'''Richard Olding Hynes''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (29 November 1944 – 6 January 2026) was a British biologist, who was a [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Investigator,<ref name=hhmi>{{cite web|title=Richard O. Hynes, PhD|url=https://www.hhmi.org/scientists/richard-o-hynes|website=Howard Hughes Medical Institute|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref> and the [[Daniel K. Ludwig]] [[Professor]] for [[Cancer]] Research at the [[Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research]], [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).<ref name=koch>{{cite web|title=Richard O. Hynes|url=http://ki.mit.edu/people/faculty/hynes|website=The Koch Institute|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref> His research focused on [[cell adhesion]] and the interactions between [[Cell (biology)|cells]] and the [[extracellular matrix]], with a particular interest in understanding molecular mechanisms of [[metastasis|cancer metastasis]].<ref name=koch /> Hynes is regarded as a co-discoverer of [[fibronectin]] molecules, a discovery that has been listed by [[Thomson Scientific]] ScienceWatch as a [[Nobel Prize]] candidate.<ref name=tr>{{cite journal|doi=10.3109/15419061.2013.857662|title=Leaders in Cell Adhesion: An Interview with Richard Hynes, Pioneer of Cell–Matrix Interactions|journal=Cell Communication & Adhesion|volume=20|issue=6|pages=139–146|year=2013|last1=Cowin|first1=Pamela|pmid=24274118 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Education==
Hynes earned his [[Bachelor of Arts#United Kingdom and Ireland|B.A.]] in 1966 and [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|M.A.]] in 1970 from the [[University of Cambridge]], both in [[biochemistry]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[biology]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1971. He worked as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[Imperial Cancer Research Fund]] from 1971 to 1974.<ref name=hhmi /><ref name=koch /><ref name="cv">{{cite web |title=RICHARD O. HYNES, PhD, FRS |url=http://web.mit.edu/ccrhq/hyneslab/extra/HynesCV6-08.pdf |publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology |access-date=7 April 2023 |archive-date=7 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407171217/http://web.mit.edu/ccrhq/hyneslab/extra/HynesCV6-08.pdf}}</ref>

==Academic career==
Hynes became a faculty member in the [[biology]] department at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in 1973 and was promoted to [[Professor|full professor]] in 1983. He was awarded [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]] Investigator status in 1988. He served as the head of the biology department from 1989 to 1991 and as the director of the MIT Center for Cancer Research from 1991 to 2001, and became the [[Daniel K. Ludwig]] Professor for Cancer Research and affiliated with the [[Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research]] in 1999. In 2004 he became an associate member of the [[Broad Institute]].<ref name=cv /><ref name=mitbio>{{cite web|title=Richard O. Hynes|url=https://biology.mit.edu/people/richard_hynes|website=MIT Biology|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

He served as the president of the [[American Society for Cell Biology]] in 2000.<ref name=cv /> He was a member of the Board of Governors of the [[Wellcome Trust]] beginning in 2007.<ref name=wellcome>{{cite web|title=Professor Richard Hynes FRS|url=http://www.wellcome.ac.uk/About-us/Organisation/Governance/Board-of-governors/Richard-Hynes/|website=Wellcome Trust|access-date=7 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708032220/http://www.wellcome.ac.uk/About-us/Organisation/Governance/Board-of-governors/Richard-Hynes/|archive-date=8 July 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He also served on the Life Sciences jury for the [[Infosys Prize]] in 2012.

Hynes also published on [[public policy]] and participated in the development of United States research guidelines for [[stem cell]] research, particularly [[embryonic stem cell]]s.<ref name=stemcells>{{cite web|title=Public Policy on Stem Cells|url=http://hynes-lab.mit.edu/publications/stemcells|website=Hynes Lab|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref>

==Death==
Hynes died on 6 January 2026, at the age of 81.<ref>[https://laskerfoundation.org/in-memoriam-richard-hynes/ In Memoriam: Richard Hynes]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Richard O. Hynes |url=https://www.aacr.org/professionals/membership/in-memoriam/richard-o-hynes/ |access-date=16 January 2026 |website=American Association for Cancer Research (AACR)}}</ref>
